name: Google Digital Wellbeing
description: Android settings for viewing device use and managing app timers, Focus mode and related routines.
platforms: Android devices; availability and labels vary by manufacturer and version
privacy: Usage and permissions details are device-specific; review current Google documentation and device settings.
limitations: Feature availability and menu names vary; some managed accounts may not support app timers.
advantages: Built-in controls; includes app timers and related wellbeing features

name: Apple Screen Time
description: Apple device settings for reviewing usage, setting app limits and scheduling downtime.
platforms: iPhone; Apple documentation also describes iPad and Mac syncing
privacy: Usage reports and cross-device settings are described in Apple's documentation; privacy specifics not stated in reviewed source.
limitations: Available controls vary by device, OS and account configuration.
advantages: Built-in schedules and app limits; can share settings across supported Apple devices

name: StayFocusd
description: Chrome extension intended to restrict time spent on selected distracting websites.
platforms: Chrome browser; current store page mentions connected Android and other browser options
privacy: Extension permissions and current data practices should be checked on the Chrome Web Store listing before installation.
limitations: Requires Chrome extension installation; availability and product details may change.
advantages: Website time restrictions in the browser

name: LeechBlock NG
description: Browser extension for scheduling site blocks and setting time limits for selected websites.
platforms: Firefox desktop and Android; other supported browsers listed by project documentation
privacy: Firefox Add-ons listing says developer reports no data collection; extension requests website access permissions.
limitations: Requires extension permissions to inspect website activity; browser support varies.
advantages: Flexible schedules, block sets, delay and lockdown controls

name: Freedom
description: Distraction blocking service for websites and apps across supported devices.
platforms: Mac, Windows, iOS, Android, Chromebook/Linux (official help page)
cost: Free tier and premium subscription; exact price not included here
limitations: Free accounts have session limits and fewer scheduling features; current terms can change.
advantages: Free tier includes blocking across supported devices; premium adds recurring and longer sessions

name: EFF Surveillance Self-Defense
description: Educational guide with practical information about privacy, surveillance and safer communications.
privacy: The guide teaches privacy and security practices; site-specific data handling not stated in reviewed source.
limitations: Some material is technical; readers can choose introductory or more advanced guides.

name: Internet Society Online Trust and Safety Hub
description: Free learning hub with guidance on scams, misinformation, privacy and security.
platforms: Web resource; hub materials support multiple languages and low-bandwidth access per launch information
privacy: Hub provides educational safety materials; site-specific data handling not stated in reviewed source.
accessibility: Designed for plain-language access and multiple languages; specific accessibility conformance not stated.
limitations: Content is educational and cannot prevent all online risks.
advantages: Practical curated learning on scams, privacy and false information

name: Firefox Enhanced Tracking Protection
description: Firefox browser feature that blocks many known trackers and other unwanted tracking elements.
platforms: Firefox desktop and mobile; exact controls vary by version
privacy: Protection settings and blocked content behavior are described by Mozilla; account-specific data handling is not stated here.
limitations: Strict settings can affect site functionality; protection does not prevent all tracking.
advantages: Built into Firefox with configurable protection levels

name: Privacy Badger
description: EFF browser extension that learns to block invisible trackers.
platforms: Firefox, Chrome, Edge and Firefox for Android per project site
privacy: Developed by EFF; current data practices and permissions should be reviewed on the official project pages.
limitations: May affect site widgets or embedded content; protection is not comprehensive.
advantages: Tracker blocking with user-facing controls; can complement built-in protections
